what_happened: The job was meant to add an auditor role that judges outcomes against BRIEF.md and the owner's goals. It was rejected with the final verdict "fail: check test failed". One check failed: in the athena-cli drain test suite, `a_change_to_max_concurrency_alone_does_not_invalidate_a_reading` failed, while 70 other tests passed. The failure output shows an athena.toml snippet with a `[parallel] max_concurrency = 1` section, which has nothing to do with the auditor work. All 8 acceptance criteria are listed as unmet. They cover the cargo test, clippy and fmt gates, the auditor role and its prompt, the brief test, the audit command, the Role round-trip, the no-warden and no-governance-file-edits criterion, and the prose-only protection note. Because the check failed, the criteria were probably not judged, so the work was not shown to be wrong on them. No blocker or major findings are listed. The stored fields do not say whether the auditor change caused the failing test or whether it already failed on the base.
cause: Nothing separates a failure the job caused from one already on the base, or from a clash with a concurrent config and test change. The check stage has no baseline run and no mapping from tests to the change. A failing check also ends the job with every criterion marked unmet, so the verdict does not say which criteria the work met. The failing test concerns the parallel max_concurrency config reading, whose fixture or expectation seems out of step with the current athena.toml and schema state. The producer could also hand over without running the full suite. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show whether the base was green.
prevention: Add a code check at admission and before handover. Admission would run the full test suite on the base commit and record which tests fail. Before handover the producer must run the same suite, and the system would compare the two. A test that fails on the base is labelled pre-existing and is fixed first as its own job or excluded from this job's verdict. A test that fails only after the change goes back to the producer to repair before the verifier starts. The verdict should list a failed check apart from the criteria, and should still judge the criteria that can be judged.
proposed_request: Make check failures attributable. Before a job starts, run the full workspace test suite on the base and record which tests fail. Before handover, run it again and diff. A test failing only after the change goes back to the producer to fix before verification. A test failing on the base is reported as pre-existing and does not decide the job's verdict. When a check fails, the verdict must still judge each acceptance criterion it can, and keep the failed check separate from the criteria. Add tests with a fake pre-existing failure and a fake newly introduced failure. Then fix `a_change_to_max_concurrency_alone_does_not_invalidate_a_reading` in the athena-cli drain tests, and re-ask the auditor role job (judged against BRIEF.md and owner goals) so it passes cargo test, clippy and fmt.
